title: 2020 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: There exists a unique strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative integers \(a_1 \lt a_2 \lt \cdots \lt a_k\) such that \[\frac{2^{289} + 1}{2^{17} + 1} = 2^{a_1} + 2^{a_2} + \cdots + 2^{a_k}.\] What is \(k?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(x = 2^{17}.\) Then \(\dfrac{2^{289} + 1}{2^{17} + 1}\) \(= \dfrac{x^{17} + 1}{x + 1}\) \(= x^{16} - x^{15} + \cdots - x + 1,\) an alternating sum of the \(17\) powers \(x^0, x^1, \ldots, x^{16}.\)

Pair each subtracted power with the added power just above it: \(x^{m+1} - x^m\) \(= 2^{17m}(2^{17} - 1)\) \(= 2^{17m} + 2^{17m+1}\) \(+ \cdots + 2^{17m+16},\) a block of \(17\) consecutive powers of \(2.\)

There are \(8\) such pairs, together with the leftover \(+2^0.\) The blocks occupy disjoint ranges, so the total number of powers is \(8 \cdot 17 + 1 = 137.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
